before.prompt: If Gold 1 follows your inward move, which response could help?

options.text: Call for a pass without looking at Gold 1
Reoffer elsewhere or make room for C
Remain still because your first move should have worked

before.explanation: A supporter should update the option; the first movement does not guarantee availability.

after.prompt: YOU want to offer D1 a shorter pass while moving nearer the middle. Looking at the players, which direction fits both aims for your first few strides?

options.text: Toward the side boards nearest YOU

after.explanation: A short move toward C brings YOU nearer D1 and nearer the middle. Do not skate all the way into C’s space: stop and check whether YOU offer a separate passing line. Moving toward Gold 2 heads inward but initially lengthens D1’s pass; moving toward the nearby boards goes wider. Those directions may serve other plans as players move.

optionReasons.reason: C direction shortens receiver-carrier distance and reduces |y|. Stop short of crowding C.
Gold 2 is an opponent direction landmark, not a receiver. Inward but initially increases pass length.
Wall-side movement increases width and pass length; plausible wide support but fails stated aims.

limitations: Advisory author; not reviewed, approved or applied.
No motion, reach, timing, gaze, collision or completed pass simulated.
Render/mobile legibility and U13 challenge require independent assessment.
Scene setup unchanged; proposed short movements are directions, not scored destinations.
Canonical carried-puck offset checked with makeScene; no rendered screenshot inspected by author.

The one-metre move toward C reduces Gold1 point clearance from 0.349 m to 0.039 m. It meets shorter/inward constraints but does not improve lane availability; independent reviewer should reject if this constrained aim teaches an unhelpful move.

geometry.units: metres; source x/y; angle in degrees
geometry.method: makeScene canonical owner-facing puck offset; Euclidean point-to-segment distances. One-metre trial positions are analysis examples only, not movement simulation or scored targets.
geometry.limits: Point clearance is not stick/body reach or interception feasibility; endpoint does not prove route safety.

imageDependency: Options require locating named players or rink landmarks relative to YOU; prompt does not supply those positions. Briefing supplies some context, so no claim that image is sole information source.
